# **⏰Polls Close in 48 Hours⏰**
---
**We are just 48 hours from finishing this thing!** My campaign has been built on three simple words: Truth, Love, & Grit. And in these final 48 hours, **I'm asking for your help speaking the truth, spreading the love, and showcasing grit across our district.**

|

Come out and join us knocking doors, making calls, driving folks to the polls, or greeting voters at the polls on Election Day. **Help me spread our philosophy of Truth, Love, & Grit and join our fight for a better Virginia!**

While we await the release of Charlie's book, please enjoy this snippet from the Foreword of **[_Stop, in the Name_ _of_](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01K93JV23VBQ234QE4SJWGXDY6_7)**[ __**God**](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01K93JV23VBQ234QE4SJWGXDY6_8), written by his wife, Erika Kirk.

|
---
| **FOREWORD BY ERIKA KIRK**
When Charlie first spoke of writing a book on the Sabbath, I felt a quiet joy rise within me. Out of all the topics the world might expect from him; politics, culture, or the crises of our day, this was not the obvious choice. And yet, it was the right one. I knew he had been entrusted with a message for weary souls. For beneath the constant hum of urgency and the endless clamor of life, he discerned what so many overlook: the absence of true rest. Not the shallow relief of sleeping late or silencing a phone, but the holy rest that comes only when one surrenders the rush, sits before the Lord, and remembers that He is God. Charlie’s days were full to the brim. He bore a weight of responsibility that few could comprehend. Charlie hosted three hours of live radio each day, traveled more than three hundred days a year, visited college and high school campuses every week, and passionately shared the Gospel at churches around the country. Layered on top of this was the sacred calling of being a husband and a father, roles he never treated lightly. By all appearances, there should have been no margin left. And yet, there was. Charlie understood that human strength alone could never sustain such a life. He anchored himself in the Word of God. He embraced the Sabbath not as an antiquated ritual, but as a bold confession of faith and a declaration that the world is upheld by God’s hand, not man’s striving. My husband’s conviction was not born in a moment, nor did it appear without root. From the earliest days of our marriage, I watched him earnestly pursue what it meant to walk in obedience to God. He was well acquainted with the lure of busyness and the subtle tyranny of distraction, as we all are, and he understood the quiet devastation they bring to families, to communities, and even to a nation. Honoring the Sabbath became his defiance against that lie. It was his declaration that a man’s value is not measured by
his output and productivity level, but by his surrender. In keeping the Sabbath, Charlie was saying with his life: “God, You are enough, and because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold.”
This book is the fruit of that conviction. In **[Stop, in the Name of](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01K93JV23VBQ234QE4SJWGXDY6_9)**[**God**](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01K93JV23VBQ234QE4SJWGXDY6_10), you will hear Charlie’s voice inviting you to recover what our
hurried culture has nearly erased. His desire was for every generation, young and old alike, to rediscover the Sabbath as he did: not as a burden to bear, but as a gift to receive. A sacred rhythm meant to draw us nearer to God, to steady our hearts with His peace, and to restore our strength for the battles to which He has called us.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3d79d002-f0fb-4f2b-a4aa-e90d150b6949?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I have been traveling quite a bit lately. The chaos of airports and dependably undependable airlines seem to be the only certainty in an increasingly uncertain world. In fact, I now plan on at least a delay if not outright cancellation and arrive at the airport with backup plans for each trip, and I regularly travel in sneakers just so I'm prepared to sprint to a connecting flight. There was once a time that traveling by plane was glamorous, when travelers dressed for the occasion, and passengers could look forward to a good meal while en route to their destination. Those days are long gone, but might they return?
The question hints at a topic that's long been a fascination of mine - cycles. In this case, we're not talking about credit cycles that result in boom-bust dynamics, but instead of social and political cycles that change our day-to-day existence and feelings.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..NRCfgQy-4Xy-5_syHGl0KXLvGKoIzknDjZQX5zMLf7Y?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=177823727)
Those who know me know that I love reading. I continue to either listen to or read at least three books a month and am often looking for connections across seemingly disparate domains. My interest in social cycles began when I read _**[The Fourth Turning: An American Prophecy- What the Cycles of History Tell Us About America's Next Rendezvous with Destiny](https://substack.com/redirect/ee877f37-1c35-45d1-ac9d-313235e0b40f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_. The book suggests, through an analysis of parenting styles and social reflections of various decades, a roughly 80-year cycle that usually ends in war or disruptive chaos during the "fourth turning." The American revolution (~1780) was followed ~80 years later by the Civil War (~1860) which was followed ~80 years later by World War II (~1940).
The book, published in 1997, suggested the 2020s would be another fourth turning and a volatile time for America. I first read the book around 2010 and remain haunted by its semi-accurate description of the world we find ourselves in today. In 2023, one of the authors penned _**[The Fourth Turning is Here: What the Seasons of History Tell Us about How and When This Crisis Will End](https://substack.com/redirect/13652ec4-a995-461d-a8a3-78c673c209f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_ , a book that suggests the 2030s will lead a moment of max crisis but also one of tremendous opportunity. Both books are worth your time.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/ef51ad12-5289-4fb3-96c2-5f4539e67187?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
While I was teaching at Harvard, I had the opportunity to meet with and discuss some of the social cycle theories with Professor Robert Putnam, author of _**[Bowling Alone](https://substack.com/redirect/e2d1da6e-b656-48e4-b514-1ad9a86728bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_ , a book that had described the social sorting of American society that resulted in the breakdown of institutions that created a shared sense of community.
He later went on to write _**[The Upswing: How America Came Together a Century Ago and How We Can Do It Again](https://substack.com/redirect/c5339a8c-8de2-4506-8cb2-69309fa01954?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_, a book in he suggested America swings in roughly 60 year cycles between an "I" society (max inequality) and a "we" society (more community oriented, less inequality). He pointed out that the extraordinary inequality of the 2020s echoed the extreme inequality of the Carnegie/Vanderbilt era roughly 120 years ago. In the middle of these two extremes was an opposite extreme, captured most clearly by President Kennedy's "Ask not what your country can do for you, but what you can do for your country." Putnam's analysis suggests the next few decades will see the emergence of a more "we" oriented society.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c2cef8a6-047e-4e38-b80d-ed0a4f2aa685?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Most recently, however, I had the opportunity to get through a book by Peter Turchin titled _**[End Times: Elites, Counter-Elites, and the Path of Political Disintegration](https://substack.com/redirect/ef0eeeb4-8b10-4760-b1f3-424efcd8fe3d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_. In it, Turchin seeks to make sense of the upheaval seen in societies around the world these days using "cliodynamics," a quantitative, data-driven approach to history.
My admittedly simplified summary of the _**End Times**_ logic is that social and political upheaval is the result of increasingly inequality combined with elite overproduction. As society becomes increasingly polarized with greater dispersion in wealth and income, it becomes increasingly important for those seeking power or wealth to has elite status. An oversupply of elites (relative to opportunities for elites) leads to instability and upheaval as elites eventually turn on themselves in the quest for limited power (there are only 100 US Senators, for instance). I find this concept compelling given the instability we have seen generated by a surplus of over-educated youth in [Bangladesh, Nepal, and Sri Lanka](https://substack.com/redirect/e3adbf44-464f-4346-a9bf-f90cab386d68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), as well as [Madagascar](https://substack.com/redirect/eb46f0db-6f9f-4e71-9373-2854c0066796?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..NRCfgQy-4Xy-5_syHGl0KXLvGKoIzknDjZQX5zMLf7Y?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=177823727)
It also appears to be the case here in the United States. American colleges and universities are churning out more college graduates than there are college-educated jobs (a phenomenon likely to be compounded by artificial intelligence). Motivated less by the cause _du jour_ (George Floyd, Israeli aggression) than by underemployment and status anxiety, a generation assured they were special are lashing out at their lot in life. These protests give them a sense of purpose and a reason for existence that they are struggling to find in employment.
Turchin's thesis can explain the Trump phenomenon as well, as a surplus of elites creates fierce competition, and those shut out become "counter-elites" that in turn challenge the established order. These counter-elites harness elite scorn to fan mass resentment. Note the way Trump leveraged Hillary's [basket of deplorables](https://substack.com/redirect/a5b805d5-c53b-49c2-a4ff-1972d775fc9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) comment and Biden calling his supporters "[garbage](https://substack.com/redirect/a5b805d5-c53b-49c2-a4ff-1972d775fc9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" and used it to fuel the MAGA movement.
So what do _**The Fourth Turning**_ , _**The Fourth Turning is Here**_ , _**The Upswing**_ , and _**End Times**_ have in common? They all provide frameworks for thinking about the future based on historical cycles and recurring dynamics. A generalist approach dictates thinking in probabilistic scenarios rather than certainties, and while I believe there is compelling evidence behind these social and demographic cycles, I think they are most useful in helping you think about possible future**s** , rather than one deterministic future.
As I've often said, each perspective is limited, biased, and incomplete...so why rely on just one? In aggregate, these frameworks for thinking about the future seem to suggest that Mark Twain had it right when he (supposedly) said, "**History does not repeat itself, but it often rhymes. "**

Can the cycles of history suggest possible futures? | | | Nov 3 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- I have been traveling quite a bit lately. The chaos of airports and dependably undependable airlines seem to be the only certainty in an increasingly uncertain world. In fact, I now plan on at least a delay if not outright cancellation and arrive at the airport with backup plans for each trip, and I regularly travel in sneakers just so I'm prepared to sprint to a connecting flight. There was once a time that traveling by plane was glamorous, when travelers dressed for the occasion, and passengers could look forward to a good meal while en route to their destination. Those days are long gone, but might they return? The question hints at a topic that's long been a fascination of mine - cycles. In this case, we're not talking about credit cycles that result in boom-bust dynamics, but instead of social and political cycles that change our day-to-day existence and feelings. Those who know me know that I love reading. I continue to either listen to or read at least three books a month and am often looking for connections across seemingly disparate domains. My interest in social cycles began when I read . The book suggests, through an analysis of parenting styles and social reflections of various decades, a roughly 80-year cycle that usually ends in war or disruptive chaos during the "fourth turning." The American revolution (~1780) was followed ~80 years later by the Civil War (~1860) which was followed ~80 years later by World War II (~1940). The book, published in 1997, suggested the 2020s would be another fourth turning and a volatile time for America. I first read the book around 2010 and remain haunted by its semi-accurate description of the world we find ourselves in today. In 2023, one of the authors penned , a book that suggests the 2030s will lead a moment of max crisis but also one of tremendous opportunity. Both books are worth your time. While I was teaching at Harvard, I had the opportunity to meet with and discuss some of the social cycle theories with Professor Robert Putnam, author of , a book that had described the social sorting of American society that resulted in the breakdown of institutions that created a shared sense of community. He later went on to write , a book in he suggested America swings in roughly 60 year cycles between an "I" society (max inequality) and a "we" society (more community oriented, less inequality). He pointed out that the extraordinary inequality of the 2020s echoed the extreme inequality of the Carnegie/Vanderbilt era roughly 120 years ago. In the middle of these two extremes was an opposite extreme, captured most clearly by President Kennedy's "Ask not what your country can do for you, but what you can do for your country." Putnam's analysis suggests the next few decades will see the emergence of a more "we" oriented society. Most recently, however, I had the opportunity to get through a book by Peter Turchin titled . In it, Turchin seeks to make sense of the upheaval seen in societies around the world these days using "cliodynamics," a quantitative, data-driven approach to history. My admittedly simplified summary of the End Times logic is that social and political upheaval is the result of increasingly inequality combined with elite overproduction. As society becomes increasingly polarized with greater dispersion in wealth and income, it becomes increasingly important for those seeking power or wealth to has elite status. An oversupply of elites (relative to opportunities for elites) leads to instability and upheaval as elites eventually turn on themselves in the quest for limited power (there are only 100 US Senators, for instance). I find this concept compelling given the instability we have seen generated by a surplus of over-educated youth in , as well as . It also appears to be the case here in the United States. American colleges and universities are churning out more college graduates than there are college-educated jobs (a phenomenon likely to be compounded by artificial intelligence). Motivated less by the cause du jour (George Floyd, Israeli aggression) than by underemployment and status anxiety, a generation assured they were special are lashing out at their lot in life. These protests give them a sense of purpose and a reason for existence that they are struggling to find in employment. Turchin's thesis can explain the Trump phenomenon as well, as a surplus of elites creates fierce competition, and those shut out become "counter-elites" that in turn challenge the established order. These counter-elites harness elite scorn to fan mass resentment. Note the way Trump leveraged Hillary's comment and Biden calling his supporters "" and used it to fuel the MAGA movement. So what do The Fourth Turning , The Fourth Turning is Here , The Upswing , and End Times have in common? They all provide frameworks for thinking about the future based on historical cycles and recurring dynamics. A generalist approach dictates thinking in probabilistic scenarios rather than certainties, and while I believe there is compelling evidence behind these social and demographic cycles, I think they are most useful in helping you think about possible futures , rather than one deterministic future. As I've often said, each perspective is limited, biased, and incomplete...so why rely on just one? In aggregate, these frameworks for thinking about the future seem to suggest that Mark Twain had it right when he (supposedly) said, "History does not repeat itself, but it often rhymes. body:
The cost of radical rot in Colorado schools
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/saufef1b1c0)
---
**November 2, 2025** **SUNDAY NEWS DIGEST**
| | Dear Readers,
This week, Rocky Mountain Voice takes a hard look at **what happens** **when ideology—not integrity—drives education**.
Nowhere is this clearer than in La Plata County, where three stories reveal how extreme liberal agendas have warped classrooms from kindergarten to college, leaving families fractured and faith in education shaken.
At Fort Lewis College in Durango, free speech collided with campus ideology. Students forming a Turning Point USA chapter hosted a respectful debate—police on standby for safety—but two weeks later, [their recognition as an official group was denied](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/s9rad79dbb0). The student government claimed the move protected “safety,” even as members admitted TPUSA had met every requirement. Flyers were torn down, slurs scribbled across posters, and Flynn said classmates told him his MAGA hat made them feel “threatened.” Yet the students refused to back down.

“Comfort can’t be the campus creed—truth takes discomfort,” said senior Jonah Flynn, who leads the chapter. Their calm resolve exposes a campus culture where safety is weaponized and diversity of thought is punished.

Down the road, the Durango 9-R School District has become [ground zero for political rot](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/s8ha3f3c823). From reinstating Pride and BLM flags to allowing students to use any bathroom by self-identification, the board has prioritized activism over academics. [Parents who question these policies are ignored](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/sfn0f2abac3), while taxpayer dollars—like the $69,000 spent on a single DEI training day—go to consultants instead of classrooms. Federal complaints allege discriminatory hiring practices, and a former teacher now faces 48 federal counts of child exploitation.
But no story captures the human toll more painfully than that of a Durango mother battling cancer, who learned that while she was fighting for her life, [a teacher had drawn her child into a relationship that blurred every boundary](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/s3l3beea42d) between classroom and home.
And at CU Boulder, that same intolerance turned violent when a conservative student leader was [targeted and assaulted](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/sbt2bc49ba0) after being listed on an [online “hit list.”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/seieeb2b174) When a culture shuts out dissent, it breeds hate—and we’re watching it unfold on Colorado campuses today.
And, ICYMI, if you haven’t followed our [12-part Douglas County Dirty Dozen investigative series](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/sas1f9a82c9), catch up now on all platforms—[Instagram](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/sbm3f321b3c), [Facebook](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/sbp0d9c468d), [X (Twitter)](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/s4pb3413c58), and [TikTok](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/s4i25ddf2c2). This week’s videos expose a district in decline—where parents who fought for school choice now face renewed attacks, a teacher accused of grooming students stayed in classrooms for years, a promised school bond produced no results, and district leaders denied new charters despite sitting on 1,000 acres of unused land. Day 11-12 are coming tonight and tomorrow!
**These stories share one root cause: a failure of leadership.** When those entrusted to educate instead indoctrinate, students suffer, families fracture, and trust erodes.
Ideology divides, but truth unites. And this Tuesday, every Coloradan has a chance to make their voice count by electing school board leaders who serve students—not agendas.
Your vote is more than a ballot—it’s a stand for reason, for accountability, and for the next generation.
In liberty and truth,
Team RMV

**[From stomachache to ideology: How Colorado’s “Right to Know” built a hospital compliance registry](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/sdv0ca8ab2c)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/s1la37a7127)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/s8ua32c37e4) Just after midnight, an 18-year-old Colorado woman—identified here as “Clarity” to protect her identity—went to the ER, hoping the pain was only a severe case of gastritis. She’s a recent high-school graduate now working for a Colorado nonprofit and was granted anonymity by RMV. __
**[Faith without votes is dead](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/sbqb40d55d4)** BY BERNIE LAKE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/s4k80ebe186) _Christians should engage in the public square. Unfortunately many are unengaged, likely because there’s been a perceived disconnect between the secular and the sacred. But, there is not. Not only is voting in our elections a civic duty, it should be an act shaped by our Christian values._
**[Free speech tested: Fort Lewis TPUSA students persevere with faith, composure—and resolve](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/sfr2132202a)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/s1j0f3c9ee1) The first Turning Point USA event, “Debate a Conservative,” took place Oct. 16 in the Fort Lewis College Student Union, where police stood at the doors as a steadying presence. Jonah Flynn, a senior studying philosophy and Spanish, along with Charlie Parke and Isabella Trevino, who were working to start a TPUSA chapter on campus, had braced for hostility but insisted on dialogue.

**[While she fought cancer, a Durango teacher moved in on her child](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/s4u725d4b86)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/s4g297d5751) When Colorado mom Cindy Stein sat before state lawmakers last spring, she was still recovering from cancer—and from losing her child to a teacher’s influence in a system that no longer sees parents as essential. “While I was fighting for my life, this teacher inserted herself into my daughter’s world, convincing her to reject me and her family,” Stein told the Senate Judiciary Committee.
**[Hospitals on life support: Report says 70% of Colorado facilities losing money](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/s4p28566437)** [DENVER GAZETTE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-6g/s0ve6b526e5) Nearly 70% of Colorado hospitals ended 2024 with “unsustainable” margins, according to a new financial report from the Colorado Hospital Association. Tom Rennell, the group’s senior vice president of financial policy and data analytics, said hospitals’ expenses are outpacing their revenue, as an increasing number of Colorado patients are losing their insurance coverage, partially due to the post-pandemic Medicaid unwind.

But then I had a deep joy—because when wicked people hate you, it means you’re doing good.”

clean_body: Democracy Docket: New Ruling Cuts Off Key Tool to Protect Minority Voters| | | Voters desperately need a "private right to action " to protect their rights. All that phrase means is that we, the people, can bring forward a lawsuit ourselves when we see wrongdoing in our elections. These 8th Circuit decisions strip us of that \-- in a world where most legal action around voting rights comes from groups like ours and our partners, not from the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ). And we've got at least these four years of DOJ's Civil Rights division facing internal attacks from a hostile presidential administration that doesn't just believe conspiracy theories, but spreads them. = | = | | Folks: An update from the federal 8th Circuit onone of the most dangerous anti-voter rulings we’ve seen in years. A federal appeals court recently cut off a key avenue for private groups and individuals to bring racial discrimination claims under the Voting Rights Act (VRA). The ruling, which applies in seven states, further weakens the ability of our civil rights law to protect voters, and could lead to the Supreme Court settling the issue. This goes back to an initial ruling from 2023, the impact of which is pretty simple to understand: That voters and voting rights organizations can no longer sue to overturn unjust laws under the Voting Rights Act. According to the 8th Circuit, and now confirmed on appeal, only the Department of Justice (DoJ) has the legal standing to sue states over voting laws. With former Florida AG Pam Bondi -- a "big lie" spreading MAGA acolyte -- serving as Attorney General, it's clear that the DOJ is not going to protect voting rights over the next four years. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | = | = | = | | = | = | = | | This is all about the legal term "private right of action". The 8th Circuit says it doesn't exist. That means the pro-voting lawsuits we've seen in states like Wisconsin, Georgia, Florida, and others nationwide wouldn't be possible anymore if the Supreme Court backs up this ruling. We won’t sugarcoat this: This could be a crushing blow to many voting rights organizations across the country, ourselves included. If this new appellate ruling is not overturned by the Supreme Court, it could unravel all of the great work pro-voting organizations are doing across the country — and allow dozens of unjust, unconstitutional voter restrictions to stand. Attacks like this on what remains of the Voting Rights Act are going to get worse over the next few years. I served our nation in the US Marine Corps as an electrician & a diesel mechanic. I kept my brothers & sisters on the move and equipped to DEFEND our nation from terrorists & communists. It was during my service that I learned what real leadership and sacrifice are. _**I am forever grateful that I had the privilege to serve and defend our nation, Fellow American.**_

There's a saying: _Once a Marine, always a Marine._ Every Marine shares the same spirit of duty and service that inspired me to join--to defend our neighbors and our nation. That's why, today, I'm still serving my country.

But now, I'm fighting for my friends' and neighbors' freedoms as a civilian. In 2021, I decided to run for Lieutenant Governor of Virginia because I saw that our nation needed a strong Christian, someone who has served this great country, to step up and LEAD!

**And after a historic and hard-fought battle, my team and I won by LESS THAN 1.6% of the vote!!** Now, Democrats want me _GONE_. It doesn't matter that I'm a patriotic Marine, a strong Christian, and a mom & grandma; _the Left can 't stand me because I am a proud and unapologetic conservative!_

Standing Up for Girls in Sports
Rep. Mike Soboleski recently spoke at a meeting of the Augusta School Board, advocating for the district to follow federal Title IX laws.
Unlike many other districts across Maine, Augusta will not comply with federal Title IX, opting to allow men to continue competing in women's sports.

Recent Op-Ed: I fear Maine is one legislative session away from becoming a sanctuary state
by Rep. Michael Soboleski in October, 2025
State Rep. Michael Soboleski is a Republican from Phillips and the founder of Maine Issues & Action PAC (MiaPAC), a political action committee that advocates for individual liberty and limited government.
This time last year, GOP candidates like myself shared our vision with voters at parades, on front porches, and in meeting halls across Maine. We did our best to contrast our vision with our opponents, describing how, in our view, we're just one legislative session away from becoming a sanctuary state.
As Democrats plan to re-purpose the second regular session -- meant only for budgetary matters and emergencies -- the people of Maine deserve to know how close we are to following the lead of California and Massachusetts. And it's not just about public safety -- sanctuary-style policies also mean Maine taxpayers could be stuck paying the bill for housing, food, medical care, and schools, while many families are already being taxed out of their homes.
The Legislature, controlled by Democrats, has already passed LD 1971, a bill that would severely restrict cooperation between local law enforcement and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
Gov. Janet Mills has delayed her decision until the next legislative session, but it is very possible that Maine could become a de facto sanctuary state by the time the 2026 midterm elections roll around.
Our state Constitution makes clear that the Maine Legislature's Second Regular Session -- the "short session" in even-numbered years -- is meant only for budgetary matters, bills held by the governor, true emergencies, or unfinished business. It was not intended as a second chance for controversial legislation.
In the early days of statehood, the Legislature sometimes didn't even convene in a given year if there was no urgent work. Contrast that restraint -- something we could use a lot more of today -- with today's overreach: declaring an "emergency" to justify a bill that could tie the hands of police and changes how our state interacts with our federal law enforcement partners.
LD 1971 would bar Maine law enforcement from detaining someone solely at ICE's request and would prevent county jails from cooperating with ICE. In practice, it essentially tells police to look the other way -- even when cooperation could protect the public.
Maine should reject becoming a sanctuary state, and I'll be working each and every day as a member of Maine's House of Representatives to stand up to this nonsense.
Sanctuary policies can prevent police from working with ICE on cases involving human trafficking, drug smuggling, or violent crime. That creates dangerous gaps criminals can exploit.
Too many families are already grappling with the opioid crisis, so why make it harder for law enforcement to coordinate across agencies and keep our communities safe?
Immigration laws are federal laws. By blocking cooperation, Maine would be signaling that some laws can be ignored based on political preference. That sets a dangerous precedent. If state leaders can pick and choose which federal laws to follow, what's next?
When ICE is prevented from taking custody of undocumented individuals, local governments are often left holding the bag. That can mean longer jail stays, higher correctional costs, and more strain on county budgets. Sanctuary policies don't save money -- they may pass the bill on to Mainers.
Maine has welcomed thousands of legal immigrants who followed the rules, filled critical workforce shortages, and enriched our communities. Sanctuary status blurs the line between legal immigration and unlawful presence. That disrespects those who played by the rules and creates resentment instead of unity.
During the public hearing for LD 1971, opponents of sanctuary cities warned that expedited removals already exist for those without proper documents. Blocking cooperation likely ensures that individuals who break immigration laws, which are sometimes committed alongside other crimes, slip through the cracks.
I'll be the first to say that Maine needs more workers, young families, and the vitality that newcomers to our state can bring, legally. But there is a difference between welcoming legal immigrants and turning Maine into a sanctuary for unlawful behavior.
If Gov. Mills lets this bill become law, I believe it will cement her legacy as being complicit in progressive social experiments -- the kind of "woke" policymaking that puts ideology ahead of our safety.
In my view, the people of Maine deserve safe communities where law enforcement can collaborate with federal partners. Those of us serving in elected office should recognize how close Maine is to becoming a sanctuary state, and the importance of standing up for the rule of law.

Add your name, and tell Trump: "No war with Venezuela!"**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T52f78556-e49c-4cd7-aa3b-4af729aabd1d/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) He has been blowing up boats without any proof of threat or wrongdoing, he has talked openly about sending secret forces in (kinda ruining the "secret" part), and he has been readying our military forces for an invasion. This would be a disaster. Venezuela is a major producer and exporter of oil (and an OPEC nation), and an attack would likely send oil prices skyrocketing. It could also spark a refugee crisis throughout the region, spurring instability that could lead to other wars. And it could lead to thousands or tens of thousands of deaths. Venezuela poses no threat to us. There is no reason to attack. Trump says it's about protecting America from fentanyl but ["there is no evidence Venezuela produces or traffics fentanyl"](https://default.salsalabs.org/Ta8006a05-b12d-4625-bb16-530ffe9549ed/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9), it's coming from other countries. | Greater Georgia Newsletter November 2025
---
| Tomorrow is Election Day in Georgia and thanks to you, Greater Georgia has helped build an incredible wave of momentum heading into the finish line.
After wrapping up a strong voter registration drive before the October 6 deadline, our team hasn't slowed down. We've been knocking on doors, making calls, and mobilizing volunteers across the state to ensure every likeminded voter knows what's at stake -- strong leadership, a thriving economy, and public servants who put Georgia families first.
Now, as we enter the final stretch, our mission is clear: Turn out every voter who shares our vision for a stronger, freer, and Greater Georgia.
---
| |
---
|
## The Final Countdown: Field Highlights and Momentum
---
|
---
On October 20, Greater Georgia shared our [County-by-County Analytics Tool](https://fsdy8nbbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018RlEBm01ztkTnz3_4lXMh4cM5LJC0xvn0QiynCMi_Wf9GTJi8FUmNQdYHTLy8Fxwhf7KT6ufLmba0PKn9nkX0eVwawN3i7Yioj2GmYXfVBqZLF9eb4N6Czh_FBdFifQdL5uVd1kHV4Ku9wLkANwpNy_-8LJT05yL_M8rWyxvZ7bCfgtke5M0XUPb-1WvX_KgoBD9cCAUJs7QizGFd3VB8XcXnLOT3tcIKqEWyJxR_WElHZAUrHxnt5InYEmh-kSeldWcerJNIMU=&c=8hc4ceXG1g0rEZPSntQcw7btvD_erHd7yDBt5FG6CqeNOLEkxoMhXA==&ch=ZV3ho7sYel1nwBF49ErxUnNC5GqGBUJrL7rrZSucf6v7aaJmj5lgrg==), highlighting that statewide turnout was below 1.4% after one full week of early voting.
With your help, we were able to successfully make 248,012 unique voter contacts to date this cycle.
Election Day is tomorrow and statewide turnout stands at 7.8%. It's not too late to join our volunteer efforts!
Contact Dylan Blitz at dylan@greatergeorgia.com to get started.
---
|
---
## Election Integrity Updates
---
|
---
Greater Georgia continues to monitor proceedings at the House Blue Ribbon Study Committee on Election Reform, as well as recommendations made by the State Elections Board.
This election cycle, we stepped up alongside Chatham County volunteers to aid voters whose [absentee ballots were lost in the mail system](https://fsdy8nbbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018RlEBm01ztkTnz3_4lXMh4cM5LJC0xvn0QiynCMi_Wf9GTJi8FUmNcQYCHCG5CdWbuPlnwgW-88D8hTEqy-rOBJKTR0YDHo_zMCEZZ09QNhofgVpBmPoxsY2rX00M6Te_l7614ApzlPMhkf2pErasXXuEs6Jt06EwTeDIeQBG4dUsAkqr7SVtIu3ubEqqO5TZYbM3-V82P8S7xYFXRsHyPjEK_UeYjoZog2dcOzl6sY4lFJri2ilog==&c=8hc4ceXG1g0rEZPSntQcw7btvD_erHd7yDBt5FG6CqeNOLEkxoMhXA==&ch=ZV3ho7sYel1nwBF49ErxUnNC5GqGBUJrL7rrZSucf6v7aaJmj5lgrg==), and conducted a thorough review of municipalities holding "separate and apart" elections.
Why does this matter? In several municipalities in Georgia, voters have to travel to two separate polling locations to participate in both their municipal election and the statewide Special Elections for PSC. While legally allowed, this is a barrier to voter participation and needed to be considered in our voter education efforts.

## 11 in Injured UK Mass Train Stabbing
A knife-wielding man [attacked passengers aboard](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDtuwzAQRE9DdRbI5Uq0CxZp1DltSoKfpU2H-kCkpdinD5QrpJhmBnjAvK-rudqU03T7tCPpGmcz0V4y1UqreX6PtpRSrXNpuj2XhVafj8YAh-4kxIlLE2zKL4NN0JEISDakhepB9OrMZXPXEDmSwl4F6VB1oXMqRNEjEp7xYn2T9EETgssjINvOIwgRVX8hjhdODDmFVOe1fcxpqneK-TVvtLZ-Hpus77UuhckPBgODYd_31jl_bAyG4wyDIaeNGAx-hPf2-BFvgbVZdVj2lHMqvWLIb6NN-Y9Y_6Vh0_AbAAD__1nacGE) a London-bound train near Huntingdon, England, on Saturday night, injuring 11 people, including two critically. The 32-year-old British suspect was [arrested for attempted murder](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGy4yAMRb8Gd8qA4NlJQbEN3dt2Sw82wmaDwQPEmfz9DvsLr1Ajjc7ce_58z982xJC23_Yg3XyeE71rpNaozK_nYWutzS5LSNvrPKmssW9m5PgFQgCXs7MhfmY1OO2JkORAWkwjinG6czns2imnHMflsd7VMvr7Ok7TY7qjlEoKt7gh6E4Tgss-KG9fq0Ih_DQ-iKsHJ6Y4udByuf3NIbWdfPzki8ptzccQ9d7aWZn8xdAwNOlz5tr6iaHpYIZGCIaGI0PzziU66BUZmtcTWrEhgW3Nrk-or3KFKxcodJGNFZ4peDpsqrDuIXZLUKieOVUC6xsVqDvBQttGDnwusFOBGDwxNEPR7nz3rzpOTPHtsCH-T9x-pPnS-C8AAP__hfaSkQ) after armed officers boarded the train. A rail staffer who intervened remains in life-threatening condition; police said his actions "undoubtedly saved people's lives." [Witnesses described](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O4yAQgJ8Gd1j82U4KikR37nI66YrbzsIwttlgsAAH5e1X7CtsMc180qeZ7_9jeijrrF__qB1kXsLkoSQHOUOczueuUkpZzbP163kcELWrm4kR1mFKMeGTUda9J9EYuQAw4A1IOvSM9sOF8GaTwghOFs27bhhIbyjXF6oJE0YJMevL3FhZbZQSXofxttOCUboM_RWIuBJAgoCxOcT2M1ifN1jcO7wgtjrsjZNbzkdC_IbYiNhYSmn35CtDbASPz4TYWJ-qMERnEBv3N96UN7iohHVVgcHW49mFYHCx2UNKkHAErZzDW4gxRLydPlu_muBxjsp6rHJW-onYqCK-3ejf3x_3AfExaGsQ_3WvUaGkfxCPJkpzFOucTf2ABFl3Zd33-flHzV-SfQUAAP__z--XqA) a "horrendous" scene as the attacker moved from car to car, slashing randomly. One survivor said the suspect told her, "the devil's not going to win," before sparing her life. British officials are urging calm as the country reels from the rare mass stabbing.
## Bessent: SNAP Could Restart Wednesday
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits could [restart](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uhDAUhE9jOlb-AcwWLtLQbdqUyOBneIl_kP3Y1d4-IldIMc2M5pNmvh7zw2LAtH3aCIZ8nhO8agAiKPP5E22tleyyYNrO44CyhsuZJZd9K0TL1ewshvfcNc54AAmqASP0IMWgR66a3Sjl3bjAyIUYBADXq3bOr1qpez-MCho0F00Iri5JdevXTgrh9XAH3t05sI6DQ8rl9p0x0Q4-vPMTym3NsQlmJzoqUx9MTkxOtMOOIVwZk9OeI1yDmJysi5iwUrGEOTE59f3YD1y1VM54tP5MDtPW1mSPdoEEHumqNcW444UhYB006_gWLf7RG_rXXU8jfwMAAP__ecJ_LA) as early as Wednesday, according to a Sunday statement from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Amid the government shutdown, SNAP benefits have not been paid out for November to the roughly 40 million Americans who use them to help pay for groceries. Bessent's statement comes after [two federal judges](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OpDAUhE9jMpD9bKAJHGxC1ptuiAx-brzjP-FHo779iLnCBJVUSV9J37_n8jQ--PT6ayJqcnlJeNWARHgs51c0tVYy6-rT6ywFjy3czQIc-laIlsvFGh8-i2qsdoiAskEtxgHEMD64bHaNg9qs7Mfx0RsxOevkQ6nercJy4dS0Nl7fNCG4vAOy6zcFQrhxmJCriSNTHK2nfHT_s0-0owuf_Maj23Jsgt6JSmXyD4OZwXxdV7eldbtHBvONZjALwWDmwGBesVZM1NJxxtLWZErrcrZtJRNLbet-ks1X6naKoTm0LZcPwddhZIq_ovHh55V-peqt4TsAAP__rQB8ww) ruled on Friday that the Trump administration must address the SNAP stoppage "as soon as possible." Bessent said the administration is complying with the orders and working to understand how to legally fund the $9.2 billion needed for November SNAP payments, while also appealing to Democratic lawmakers to reopen the government.
## Most Common Last Name in Every Country
The [international surname analysis](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDuOpDAYhE9jMiM_wNCBg03IetMNkRv_Bu_4JfvvRtx-xFxhglJJpVKV9P17rk_jg0_7XxNBo8trgrMFQIS6vr-iaa2heb182t-lQN3CnayCiZFyTplcrfHhWofOagcgQHag-aQEV9PMZHfohxXKzdJyLpjlo5rn0Umn5nHe-AAv1nl9r3HO5C0h-3EbBOduUg9gw4MBGRhYj7n2_7NPeIALV_5A7bccu6APxNKI_EPEQsRynmcfIaEJLuTW7g4Ryw55r6YcFxFLNKXdlhvSLceYEw2mIU0mAvWJwgfqRbf8TlgvGk3pqrbl9CH4piYysD0aH37O8VfEPlp8BwAA__8vN4Fh) shows that the occupational name Smith is the most frequent last name in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Australia. Globally, inherited ancestral names are the most dominant type, represented by names like Sweden's Andersson and Mexico's Hernandez. The survey revealed several unique meanings and origins, including the Democratic Republic of the Congo's most common surname, Ilunga, a praise-name meaning a person who forgives the first two abuses but never the third. In Finland, the most common name is Korhonen, which translates to "old hard-of-hearing person." See [the last name map here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL_u3CAMx58m2X4RGEIuA0OXTL2uHSMIJkfLvwJ36fXpKyq1L9DBkvX152NZ_nrf78p5F88vKqBsNu0Rr-qxNSz783tQtdamtHbxfOaM5fA92YHA_EHpB2G7Uc6_dz4aaREB2YiSLgKoWG6EjQ9pZys0MmuJFhT5ylYxg1n1oQXlWpPRyb6NUsJ6AZvmgwOldhErEr4SHDhB41oq07fkYnug9e_0wjIdKYxePlrLdWCfBtgG2FxQJ1aYgovPhgGNU4eJHf07HGB7Zp-UGWB70YVyfptXyv65PU6-qZ_3Ln92uqjyHmALoeZUWu8wNuWtT7XDhD6uH3Gu4vargIIm8kWmHM-xSJMv572rYhk4OYNy_s_N7b8e_ZLwOwAA__8eVZK7).

name: Rural Americans United
subject: Why Washington’s Fourth District May Hold the Line for American Democracy
body:
District 4 may now be the key battleground where Washington’s pro-democracy movement proves that rural voices can still shape the nation’s future.
| | | | |
---
| What Is In This Newsletter?

* 14,152! Together, We're Reaching New Voters
* Why Washington's Fourth District May Hold the Line for American Democracy
* Progressive Strategies: Data
* The Hatch Act Is Dead -- And So Is Accountability in Washington DC

---
| 14,152!

### Together, We're Reaching New Voters

This October, Rural Americans United is mailing 14,152 pro-democracy postcards to newly registered voters across Washington State ahead of the election.
Why newly registered voters
Because this constituency is made up primarily of young people and members of the Latinx community, two groups that have been historically underrepresented in the political process. Our data shows two troubling trends:

1. These voters are less likely to cast ballots, and
2. They are increasingly being targeted by far-right messaging.

Our goal is simple: to make sure the first political message these new voters receive is one that celebrates participation, inclusion, and democracy. By the end of 2025, we will have mailed nearly 50,000 pro-democracy messages across the state. But we are not stopping there. Our next phase includes expanding into social media, radio, and billboards to reach even more rural voters and strengthen civic engagement.
You make this possible
Your continued support allows us to amplify rural voices, empower new voters, and protect democracy in communities that are too often overlooked.
---
| | [Your Donation Is Important](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018dsutLzCUpnP6V_kwGcZ5aCGjH_lzGZUcpbqZHsHBULjHL-HpFQOpT7fBApza9Ojzn7W7sF0uZeT4ww9EB3vM_MSyrLnepepF7WMrdyX8FWLy84hRP7NY-Cez5Ial3uaD-j3Ldv_YR-H0So2PX_gBk407hE1MtRc-llbcdR7Mx6OvBjfJvhDYohKm1T8edfVIcd0lBnTwwOpXSSJnqi54TuJTNvHUtoWunxcYceGIH0=&c=182nbdcJ7lHjRtYKJS48ZhOJJ7e4FUBMljRVAAfKCMVImJ7pl6fP_w==&ch=a6rFGCBWbQ-ikHG2T1t2xy_7MCkKUWdEFmxG-K-Hhf7ndEpLgeuYlg==)
---
| |
---
|
## Why Washington's Fourth District May Hold th Line for American Democracy

If you are one of the many people who believe Washington State's Congressional District 4 is not a fight worth taking seriously, as it has not been for the last thirty years, you are dangerously mistaken. Unlike many other states, we have a real chance to make a stand and a meaningful difference.
"47" loudly and proudly declared during his 2024 presidential bid that if people voted for him, they would never have to vote again. That was not a warning shot across the bow; it was the opening salvo of a MAGA revolution. Steve Bannon recently echoed this in an interview with [The Economist](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018dsutLzCUpnP6V_kwGcZ5aCGjH_lzGZUcpbqZHsHBULjHL-HpFQOpeq6MSH-VNn9wthlE4_3-9ZOXIAEE29Ly7djgs2C_7rXZd2bqtQOH4qwTaHj7D-ciPFlPKLYZR7X1CnfWf7mb-s1k66hQChdjnoAKF39YcK2x0qkK8oQpqPInsrMDgtrig==&c=182nbdcJ7lHjRtYKJS48ZhOJJ7e4FUBMljRVAAfKCMVImJ7pl6fP_w==&ch=a6rFGCBWbQ-ikHG2T1t2xy_7MCkKUWdEFmxG-K-Hhf7ndEpLgeuYlg==), stating that "47 will be president in 2028 because of divine providence."
Washington State remains a stronghold of democratic values and may be one of the few states left where fair and just elections will continue to be held. So far, "47" has not called in the Idaho National Guard to occupy Spokane or Seattle as he has attempted to do in other Democratic cities such as Memphis, Los Angeles, Chicago, Portland, and Washington, D.C.
Frighteningly, "47," despite his complete disconnect from reality, has proven disturbingly effective at turning his fantasies into our, very real, nightmares.
In addition to his unthinkable efforts to deploy the National Guard into American cities, there have been even more ominous moves within his vanguard. These dangerous and outrageous actions include, but are not limited to, requesting a standing militia of 500 "quick reaction troops" per state, ready to be deployed to American cities at a moment's notice ([The Hill)](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018dsutLzCUpnP6V_kwGcZ5aCGjH_lzGZUcpbqZHsHBULjHL-HpFQOpeq6MSH-VNn9_BiNbPJUu2a-msTa4ThvipT4oUNZDP3JDRZdQEQhxXH7zQvBMs-ibiw7zPw87Eq8a8kxxhE9VIYTRC7Pwc-raid4UKkaoYab8dlIxaRWmvIpWgWyBLpfSMS-DuG9HpJCxe60wukqMcZZXtCrAOXN2MqBhqHcK3ozbxfvHGwhx-mskT4bsCmfIvaUzDhzLiFOfdCttwe5jZEP30uPdLUB9g==&c=182nbdcJ7lHjRtYKJS48ZhOJJ7e4FUBMljRVAAfKCMVImJ7pl6fP_w==&ch=a6rFGCBWbQ-ikHG2T1t2xy_7MCkKUWdEFmxG-K-Hhf7ndEpLgeuYlg==). [CBS News](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018dsutLzCUpnP6V_kwGcZ5aCGjH_lzGZUcpbqZHsHBULjHL-HpFQOpeq6MSH-VNn9dKo59roG-ph-GffwmJk251CqJ4mph5twnWXMrHx0nTiUdmukpwzhR-PlMl1BI8GVsSTeODOFEapUSWJH5PsMR646TJ2Nz0la7lqK3sAq_koTLslL7KCThgRyHDK1YRb0TRWCQi3CZJQb3xN2EiD2TgAGuNOut_9DPkGuuD_lORDov-CA1r6KPd3cstTGsT30&c=182nbdcJ7lHjRtYKJS48ZhOJJ7e4FUBMljRVAAfKCMVImJ7pl6fP_w==&ch=a6rFGCBWbQ-ikHG2T1t2xy_7MCkKUWdEFmxG-K-Hhf7ndEpLgeuYlg==) also reported that "47," referring to the Insurrection Act, claimed he could send the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Marines into American cities and that the courts would not stop him. His use of the Insurrection Act is a biting irony. "47" has demanded that Republican-held states gerrymander their congressional maps to favor Republicans, and he has instructed the [DOJ to deploy election observers](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018dsutLzCUpnP6V_kwGcZ5aCGjH_lzGZUcpbqZHsHBULjHL-HpFQOpeq6MSH-VNn9Lyn9-RBRrLUwpjX2APT9OnraqzRb83seQCqGvdtN54AZxNTLNT6oGwPKlxspZw4eUG2RY60x984IOpro137RrySS3oAGNqrZ9PFlRbLSSjp0hsQd-_6cGdVVON9iSWgmdTfPYNxuuu9CXXl6uqXUooYXpFtUgnWR88SrQANv-7IJxyB3xkwK2WWLT5GJ_QNvmuJJ7SNovWQ=&c=182nbdcJ7lHjRtYKJS48ZhOJJ7e4FUBMljRVAAfKCMVImJ7pl6fP_w==&ch=a6rFGCBWbQ-ikHG2T1t2xy_7MCkKUWdEFmxG-K-Hhf7ndEpLgeuYlg==) as if we were a banana republic. These actions are unprecedented, unnecessary, and, if not entirely illegal, certainly trample on the line of legality.
At the congressional level, Washington State has consistently punched above its weight. With Representative Dr. Kim Schrier successfully holding Congressional District 8 and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez flipping Congressional District 3, we have already seen that it can be done. We now need a victory in Congressional District 4, and it can be won, but it requires serious people doing serious work to make it happen.
In the last election cycle, we had two capable candidates who both failed to launch. This cycle, we again have a strong candidate, but their campaign has yet to show clear momentum. I have personally reached out to encourage people to do what is necessary, but to date, I have heard only faint rumblings. Taking back at least one chamber of Congress is not a loss we can afford. Our country and our way of life hang in the balance, and the scales are tipping in the wrong direction. Now is not the time to look off into the distance at races far away; it is time to focus on what is attainable here and now. We can flip Congressional District 4. We can.

The data and narrative below is provided by Progressive Strategies Northwest
Voter Turnout
As the saying goes, "all politics are local." And in years where most politics are local -- odd-numbered years, in Washington State -- "local effects" matter a lot.
Rural, working-class counties number among Washington's lowest- and highest- turnout counties. Southeastern Washington's diminutive Columbia (56.7% historic turnout, county seat Dayton) and Garfield (52.8%, Pomeroy) are near the top of the list; yet, demographically similar counties are also near the bottom, including Skamania (34.0%, Stevenson) and Pend Oreille (34.3%, Newport). What explains the difference? Rigorous demographic analysis suggests: County and city-level elections in Garfield and Columbia seem to excite voters in a way they don't in Skamania and Pend Oreille.

---
| |
---
Still, demographics do matter. Ballot returns among Hispanic voters lag across elections, especially in odd years. That's a common finding across the United States -- and a major concern for voter turnout advocates. It's also a big factor driving the rankings of Yakima (27.9%) and Franklin (29.3%) counties -- although Washington's most Latino county, Adams County (35.0%), is only slightly below state average. This year -- local matters!
---
Bluest Cities
Rural Washington has a reputation as "deep red", but the reality is more complex. Outside of the Puget Sound metro core, Washington State tilts red, but by a margin of only about 55-45%. It also contains many deep-blue islands, which provide important insights into rural voting patterns.
In past years, this list would have been dominated by Hispanic and Native American communities. The #1 entry, technically more Democratic than Seattle, remains the Colville Reservation's Nespelem (Harris 46, Trump 2, Other 1). As Democrats have sustained losses among Hispanic voters, formerly top-ranking towns have fallen down the list, including Mabton (73.7%), Wapato (68.5%), Mattawa (68.3%), and Toppenish (66.4%).
---

| |

The Hatch Act Is Dead -- And So Is Accountability in Washington DC
A pamphlet published by the [Department of Justice](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018dsutLzCUpnP6V_kwGcZ5aCGjH_lzGZUcpbqZHsHBULjHL-HpFQOpeq6MSH-VNn9CjOdTR7B4Vvb4UBUAM89W5Du3D9MHbVJHD6I593pxqBl8B7JZ1iSpHdoBkHDEtL4VxAKl_OR4u0Kc6HHE-T4e533tAeumG30gdJqLLrlQzlLPAmvkAR8snT9GqBbx6Rc&c=182nbdcJ7lHjRtYKJS48ZhOJJ7e4FUBMljRVAAfKCMVImJ7pl6fP_w==&ch=a6rFGCBWbQ-ikHG2T1t2xy_7MCkKUWdEFmxG-K-Hhf7ndEpLgeuYlg==) in January 2024 defines the Hatch Act as:
"The Hatch Act generally prohibits federal employees from engaging in partisan political activity while on duty, in a federal facility, or using federal property. Political activity is defined as any activity directed toward the success or failure of a political party, candidate for partisan political office, or partisan political group."
It is easy to see why this law matters. It is meant to protect the integrity of government service from political manipulation. But under an administration that denies the rule of law and fills key positions with loyalists rather than qualified public servants, this safeguard has been trampled. Visit almost any federal website today and you will find a banner blaming Democrats for the government shutdown. Earlier in the week, the message even claimed the shutdown was due to Democrats pursuing healthcare for illegal immigrants and "gender mutilation." That line has since been softened to simply call it a "Democrat led shutdown," but the damage is done. The propaganda is blatant, and while it would be laughable in its absurdity, it is instead terrifying because so many Americans believe it.
Why is this allowed to continue? The answer lies in Project 2025. One of its primary objectives was to replace influential government officials with unwavering loyalists. The Hatch Act is enforced by the Office of Special Counsel, which at the time of 47's inauguration was led by Hampton Dellinger, a Biden nominee confirmed by the Senate. Dellinger was immediately targeted and fired.
A lawsuit followed, as the president cannot legally dismiss the head of the Office of Special Counsel or many other officials without cause. But the Supreme Court, corrupted and compliant, sided with 47, ruling that such protections limited his executive power. Soon after, the same Court granted 47 nearly unlimited authority and immunity, declaring that he, and he alone, was above the law.
And where are the Democrats? As usual, standing on the sidelines, issuing press releases with trembling lips and "stinging rebuttals." The only formal response I found was from [Senator Raskin](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018dsutLzCUpnP6V_kwGcZ5aCGjH_lzGZUcpbqZHsHBULjHL-HpFQOpeq6MSH-VNn9HT8WE8AN0XvP04xpZFl1ok3PkOcwN2eDpasJHenzPWmb3z8ampmaH2xsoF8NRuAjPiznA2XtB-6rw0h0O6FOFUwO6sVqQQ3armEAA957QcPlZOmQ3k6gl80h73BjWffmAttqyPh_aQ1WnfXghlAMc6r3mKLU-MkUMag0_eO2sPUaGU_dsiBzsYmXO8R1IKAzRDR5r5ZxEc5Dwd2F2RLceq0f3QpjQsKB3T1FX-TplhUlYlvfnwN3gEvlYtEptImvf3K4MakL56M=&c=182nbdcJ7lHjRtYKJS48ZhOJJ7e4FUBMljRVAAfKCMVImJ7pl6fP_w==&ch=a6rFGCBWbQ-ikHG2T1t2xy_7MCkKUWdEFmxG-K-Hhf7ndEpLgeuYlg==), who said the actions "may be a breach of the Hatch Act." May be? That is like saying birthright citizenship is "open for debate." The violation is clear and undeniable. Since Dellinger's unlawful dismissal, there has been a sad procession of acting heads at the Office of Special Counsel because the only nominee put forward by 47, Paul Ingrassia, is so disreputable that even Republicans refuse to confirm him.
This is more than just another political scandal. It exposes a deep failure in how we enforce laws, especially against those who make or interpret them. Violations of the law bring no consequences, only press statements and public scolding. Our "independent" agencies and counsels are proving to be anything but independent. As 47 replaces oversight with obedience, he continues to fire at will and appoint without restriction.
Acting heads do not require Senate approval, and that suits him perfectly. It allows him to install whoever he wants, without resistance or accountability. Why would he ever seek approval when he already behaves as if he needs none?
The death of the Hatch Act symbolizes something larger: the decay of accountability itself. Once a guardrail against corruption, it now stands as a hollow reminder of what used to restrain power. Unless Congress reclaims its authority and the people demand the restoration of independent oversight, this will not stop. The erosion of law is not gradual anymore; it is deliberate and accelerating. If America cannot uphold its own laws against those who govern, then the idea of a government by the people is already gone.

| Peter,
There are less than 24 hours until the November 4th Pennsylvania Supreme Court Election and Democrats are neck and neck with the GOP.
Our army of paid and volunteer canvassing are one of the only things standing in the way of a catastrophic defeat for Democrats that would all but guarantee permanent GOP control of Pennsylvania for the next decade and beyond.
These canvassers are knocking over 10,000 doors per day in cold weather pushing it to the absolute limit for Pennsylvania's Democratic justices. They are coming in from across Philadelphia and every corner of Pennsylvania, some have even drove in from as far as Maine to help us get out the vote.
Over the weekend, a local donor saw pictures online from one of these canvasses and reached out offering to place an order of large pizzas, from a local pizza joint for a canvas happening that day.

| | | | Although anecdotal, by days end the crew that received the pizza put up record numbers in a key Philadelphia precinct where we lag in turnout:
As Napoleon put it, an army marches on its stomach. With experts projecting that this race could be determined by as little as a fraction of a point, pizza could truly have a decisive impact here.

Friend,
---
So many kind souls like you have asked how I’m doing, so I wanted to personally update you on my recovery.
---
I was hospitalized after a devastating car crash. We were struck by a vehicle going what felt like 70-80 miles per hour. Had I not been wearing a seatbelt, I would’ve been killed.
---
Right now, a back brace is holding my fractured spine together.**
---
But if I could survive being arrested in the most violent jail in America, I know I can survive **__ANYTHING!__**

---
One thing especially helped take the pain away...
---
...**President Trump has announced that he will award me with the Presidential Medal of Freedom – _the highest civilian honor in America._**
---

**Left with no pardon, no safety net, and no lifeline, my _ONLY_ chance at walking free is to secure a top-notch defense team.**
---
But the reality is, the Left had already forced me to the point of **BANKRUPTCY**.
---
**And now, this car crash has set me back even more...**
---
And so, my last remaining hope of assembling the quality of defense required to BEAT the Left’s sham charges and WIN the trial of my life is patriots like _YOU_.
---
That’s why I’m making a final plea to humbly ask that you contribute whatever amount you can to my Legal Defense Trust as I continue fighting for my _FREEDOM_ and my _JUSTICE_.

__Because when President Trump places the Medal of Freedom around my neck, I want history to always remember that I FOUGHT for my freedom and justice until the VERY END!__

# Fight the Oligarchy: Vote YES for Prop 50
---
| |

Friends, tomorrow, we Californians will decide whether we will use the power of our vote to counter a brazen power grab.
When President Trump told Texas Governor Abbott to “get me five more Republican seats,” it wasn’t about fair maps — it was about rigging the game. President Trump was desperate. His policies were unpopular. His approval rating even with people who voted for him is tanking. His policies have made lives harder for working Americans and people are angry.
Our lives have progressively gotten worse:
– We can hardly afford groceries,
– We’re buried under crushing debt,
– We risk losing healthcare.
And time and time again, the powerful ruling elites are laughing their way to the bank while we are left scrambling for pennies.
This is not a battle between the left or the right. The struggle is between us, hardworking Americans vs. the ruling elites. So ask yourself: Should you stand by while billionaires and their pet politicians consolidate power — or do you fight back?
Stand up! Stand up for us, stand up for all of us Americans, and fight this corrupt billionaire takeover of our government.
Vote YES on Prop 50.

Thanks for reading this newsletter. I ordinarily write about what's on my mind with an eye toward what's happening out there.
So what's happening out there? Well, there's a federal shutdown on that is cutting off food stamps to tens of millions of American families - about 1 out of 8 families rely on SNAP benefits each month. Two federal judges ruled that the government has to tap emergency funds to pay for SNAP, but it's unclear how much money is going to get out or when it will reach people, many of whom have already been notified that they won't get money this month. Also, healthcare premiums are spiking for millions because the government reduced subsidies for Obamacare and the new rates hit on Saturday.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/60e85cbb-b8e6-483a-a100-050842a5eda6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I thought that reason would prevail and that both sides would come to the table before the weekend. After all, why incur all of this hurt, suffering and confusion just to revisit it 48 or 72 hours later?
Things are even worse than I thought. And I thought they were pretty bad. I do think the shutdown gets resolved early this week, but for millions, the damage will have been done.
I've had a grim and haunting thought a lot in the past 72 hours: the poor don't matter in America.
I felt the same way when the enhanced child tax credit - which had cut child poverty in half in 2021 - was allowed to lapse at the beginning of 2022. "We pulled you out of poverty . . . and now you're heading back down" was the message to millions of American families. There were no protests. Not more than a few press mentions. Just a return to misery.
It's happening again.
I've felt like it's not getting enough attention that millions of the most cash-strapped Americans are having food stamps cut off for the first time in modern history. Look, on a day-to-day basis most journalists aren't themselves reliant on SNAP to pay for food - I get that. But even in the media, it seems like this is being treated as a more normal story instead of an historic dereliction of responsibility.
Also this past week, Amazon announced layoffs of 14,000 white-collar workers due to AI, which will set off similar moves at other companies.
Just about every day, someone says to me some version of, "Well, you called AI eating jobs back when no one was talking about it."
I wrote '[The War on Normal People](https://substack.com/redirect/80127d5c-b84e-4350-a77e-c3a04f601e31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)' back in 2018. My fear back then was that as AI kicked in, we would start turning on each other. I wrote, "Increasing levels of desperation will lead to destabilization . . . the best-case scenario is a hyper-stratified society like something out of _The Hunger Games_ , the worst case is widespread despair, violence and the utter collapse of our society and economy." Maybe it seemed a little bit dystopian back then, but it's aging well.
One outgrowth of AI is an increasing skepticism of capitalism. As I wrote in TWoNP,
"Capital and efficiency will prefer robots, software, AI and machines to people more and more. Capitalism is like our mentor and guiding light, to whom we've listened for years. He helped us make great decisions for a long time. But at some point, he got older, teamed up with his friend technology, and together they became more extreme. They started saying things like 'Ah, let's automate everything' and 'If the market doesn't like it, get rid of it' which made reasonable people increasingly nervous. Even the most hard-nosed businessperson should recognize that the gains and losses from unprecedented technological advances will have dramatic sets of winners and losers, and that the system needs to account for that in order to continue. Capitalism doesn't work that well if people don't have any money to buy things or if communities are degenerating into scarcity, anger and despair."
I'm appearing on the news a lot this week to talk about the mayoral race and the rise of Zohran Mamdani. My response in 2020 was to run for President on the idea that government could do much more to alleviate poverty.
Instead, we're doing less. Dysfunction is increasingly the norm. Just play to your team and ignore the rest. These are sad days.

I ordinarily write about what's on my mind with an eye toward what's happening out there. So what's happening out there? Well, there's a federal shutdown on that is cutting off food stamps to tens of millions of American families - about 1 out of 8 families rely on SNAP benefits each month. Two federal judges ruled that the government has to tap emergency funds to pay for SNAP, but it's unclear how much money is going to get out or when it will reach people, many of whom have already been notified that they won't get money this month. Also, healthcare premiums are spiking for millions because the government reduced subsidies for Obamacare and the new rates hit on Saturday. | | ---|---|--- I thought that reason would prevail and that both sides would come to the table before the weekend. After all, why incur all of this hurt, suffering and confusion just to revisit it 48 or 72 hours later? Things are even worse than I thought. And I thought they were pretty bad. I do think the shutdown gets resolved early this week, but for millions, the damage will have been done. I've had a grim and haunting thought a lot in the past 72 hours: the poor don't matter in America. I felt the same way when the enhanced child tax credit - which had cut child poverty in half in 2021 - was allowed to lapse at the beginning of 2022. "We pulled you out of poverty . . . and now you're heading back down" was the message to millions of American families. There were no protests. Not more than a few press mentions. Just a return to misery. It's happening again. I've felt like it's not getting enough attention that millions of the most cash-strapped Americans are having food stamps cut off for the first time in modern history. Look, on a day-to-day basis most journalists aren't themselves reliant on SNAP to pay for food - I get that. But even in the media, it seems like this is being treated as a more normal story instead of an historic dereliction of responsibility. Just about every day, someone says to me some version of, "Well, you called AI eating jobs back when no one was talking about it." I wrote '' back in 2018. My fear back then was that as AI kicked in, we would start turning on each other. I wrote, "Increasing levels of desperation will lead to destabilization . . . the best-case scenario is a hyper-stratified society like something out of The Hunger Games , the worst case is widespread despair, violence and the utter collapse of our society and economy." Maybe it seemed a little bit dystopian back then, but it's aging well. One outgrowth of AI is an increasing skepticism of capitalism. As I wrote in TWoNP, "Capital and efficiency will prefer robots, software, AI and machines to people more and more. Capitalism is like our mentor and guiding light, to whom we've listened for years. They started saying things like 'Ah, let's automate everything' and 'If the market doesn't like it, get rid of it' which made reasonable people increasingly nervous. For months Democrats had been on track to lose this election but over the past few days the tide has turned. For the first time in this election Democrats are on the offensive.

clean_body: MAGA is panicking which is why last night President Trump took to Truth social to beg his voters to show up and vote down Pennsylvania’s “woke justices.” | | | | | == | Peter, The 2025 Pennsylvania Supreme Court election has become the penultimate set piece battle of Trump's 2nd term. On the line is control of key swing state Pennsylvania and its 19 electoral college votes. If MAGA's electoral coup succeeds they become the umpire for all elections held in PA and they can rewrite the rule book to ensure Democrats never win PA again. This is how Trump gets his 3rd term. For months Democrats had been on track to lose this election but over the past few days the tide has turned. Obama, DNC Chair Ken Martin, and PA Governor Shapiro, have come in massively to turn out the vote. Millions of Democratic small dollar donors are flooding the race with millions. For the first time in this election Democrats are on the offensive. MAGA is panicking which is why last night President Trump took to Truth social to beg his voters to show up and vote down Pennsylvania's "woke justices." | == | | | | When Trump tells his base to vote they listen. This will give MAGA a massive turnout boost. There is no doubt about it. But we can mitigate its impact. Last week, Defend our Courts placed a massive last minute $500k TV and digital ad buy to help spread the message that the only way to protect abortion in Pennsylvania is by voting Yes. It was money we technically didn't have (we owe nearly $500k to vendors). While we were able to recoup that money over the weekend, Trump's intervention means we once again need to spend our entire warchest, this time on rapid response texts and hyper targeted digital ads to turnout our voters, and once again we will need to quickly recoup that money to remain financially solvent. We've done it before and we must do it again today. | | | | Friends,

As the government shutdown drags on, the ripple effects are hitting close to home for service members, military families, and veterans, for whom:
* Training is [postponed](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=063406627f&e=33f53a5b1a).
* On-base childcare and family services have been [scaled back or paused entirely](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=f9ca9d6013&e=33f53a5b1a).
* Access to counseling and case management services through the VA's Veteran Readiness and Employment program [has stopped](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=41b5ae6647&e=33f53a5b1a).

While we welcomed the news that [service members received another round of paychecks](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=31418af502&e=33f53a5b1a), Axios reports that the Defense Department pulled money from other accounts, which normally fund [military housing, research and development, and Navy shipbuilding](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=15c5bf4f3d&e=33f53a5b1a).

This shutdown is more than a policy impasse; it’s a real strain on the people who keep our nation strong. Service members, military families, and veterans deserve stability and support, not uncertainty. We remain committed to working across the aisle to promote stability, support national security, and ensure our government upholds its responsibility to those who serve.
---
|
---
|
# Veterans Housing Legislation Nears the Finish Line
---
| [ ](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=a7086f19f6&e=33f53a5b1a)
---
| We’re excited to share that the VA Loan and Informed Disclosure (VALID) Act is currently under negotiation to be included in the final version of this year's National Defense Authorization Act. This important bipartisan legislation will help veterans and service members make more informed homebuying decisions by ensuring lenders clearly show how the VA Home Loan offers lower interest rates, no down payment, and reduced closing costs. The With Honor Action team has championed this effort for nearly 6 years, working with the Veterans Association of Real Estate Professionals and the For Country Caucus to make homeownership more accessible for our service members and veterans.
---
| [Read more about the VALID Act](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=4737aa5a9d&e=33f53a5b1a "Read more about the VALID Act")
---
|
---
|
# With Honor Action Backs SHIPS for America Act
---
| [ ](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=05028fa2ad&e=33f53a5b1a)
---
_With Honor Action ally Senator Dan Sullivan chaired the hearing titled "Sea Change: Reviving Commercial Shipbuilding"_
| With Honor Action submitted a Statement for the Record in support of the SHIPS for America Act during a Senate hearing held last week, emphasizing the urgent need to revitalize America’s shipbuilding industry, not only to strengthen our commercial capabilities, but also to bolster the Navy and our national security. Maritime security and rebuilding the maritime industrial base remain vital areas of bipartisan cooperation, with veterans and With Honor Action allies Senator Mark Kelly and Senator Todd Young leading the charge in Congress.
---
| [Read our full Statement for the Record](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=7d5a90bfcb&e=33f53a5b1a "Read our full Statement for the Record")
---
|
---
|
# With Honor x HFX Peace With Women Fellows
---
|
---
| On Thursday, With Honor Action’s Vice President of Government Affairs, Sean McClintock, met with the distinguished fellows of the Halifax International Security Forum’s Peace With Women Fellowship—a program that brings together senior female military officers from NATO and partner nations to foster dialogue on leadership, security, and collaboration in advancing peace. Their discussion centered on the crucial role of women’s leadership in enhancing international security and fostering cooperation among democracies.

body:
As SNAP funding remains uncertain, here are places you can get food, and places where you can give and volunteer to help. | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/andreahunley/events-for-democracy-october-november-18253147?e=d9ebccf591)
---
| |
---
| |
# FOOD RESOURCES IN DISTRTIC 46
This week, we are faced with the expiration of SNAP funding due to the refusal of the Trump administration to allocate emergency funds to continue the program. While I fight in the Senate for state funding to support the Hoosiers who need food most, I know that our families cannot wait for the government to act. I’ve included here some resources for anyone who needs help.

For those of us who are able, now is also a critical time to give. The list of local pantries is also a great space to see where you can volunteer and donate. The United Way has partnered with our biggest food banks to create the Central Indiana Food Relief Fund to coordinate donations, you can donate to them at [this link](https://andreahunley.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=5c2b34b98b419cb5ca0511f25&id=a7f1af395f&e=d9ebccf591). We need everyone to pitch in to keep our community from hunger until SNAP funding is restored.

**Where you get help:**
* Find food pantries, meals and more by searching your address in the [Community Compass](https://andreahunley.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=5c2b34b98b419cb5ca0511f25&id=6c33a2c04e&e=d9ebccf591).
* Search Gleaner’s list of pantries [here](https://andreahunley.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=5c2b34b98b419cb5ca0511f25&id=f00e12d3d3&e=d9ebccf591).
* The City of Indianapolis will also be running 10 food giveaways this month, you can find information about them and Indy Park’s food programs [here](https://andreahunley.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=5c2b34b98b419cb5ca0511f25&id=d41c6efd99&e=d9ebccf591).

I've also included a schedule of food pantries open weekly in district 46. Please check with the pantry about what areas they serve and what their ID requirements are.

The list of local pantries is also a great space to see where you can volunteer and donate. It feels like every year we say the same thing: _this is the most consequential election of our lives._ But this time, the weight feels heavier. With an authoritarian-style power grab unfolding in Washington, this election will be the first real test of Democratic strength during the second Trump presidency.
